uncited: This family comprises specific objective functions used to optimize the parameters of a neural radiance field during differentiable volume rendering.

While the parent family [Regularization and Loss Functions](8586-regularization-and-loss-functions.md) defines the general mechanism of gradient flow through the rendering integral, these specific formulations address distinct training goals: photometric fidelity ([Final Loss Function](15455-final-loss-function.md)), geometric plausibility via distortion minimization ([NeRF-XL Multi-GPU Distortion Loss](10377-nerf-xl-multi-gpu-distortion-loss.md)), representation efficiency ([Rate-Distortion Optimization Loss](14672-rate-distortion-optimization-loss.md)), and structural or semantic constraints ([Geometric and Structural Regularization](16814-geometric-and-structural-regularization.md)).

They are distinguished from sibling methods like [Diffusion-regularized NeRF](7381-diffusion-regularized-nerf.md) by their direct reliance on rendered pixel/depth statistics or explicit geometric priors rather than external generative priors.
Without geometric adaptation, FrugalNeRF falls short of FreeNeRF when using only single-scale loss.
The specific loss formulations described here originate from various recent advances in differentiable rendering and neural scene representation.
